slate.name: Slate
slate.hub.title: Slate
slate.hub.edit_layout.tip: Open the layout editor on the screen behind this one (needs dev mode)
slate.hub.no_modules.body: Slate UI, Multiplayer, Chat and Config each add a card here. Core alone restyles vanilla screens and provides the toolkit.
slate.settings.title: Slate settings
slate.settings.dev_mode.tip: Adds the pencil button to editable screens and enables the F7 layout editor
slate.settings.dev_pencil.tip: Where dev mode puts its pencil button, which opens the layout editor. Hidden takes it away: the editor key (F7 unless changed in Controls) opens the editor all the same.
slate.settings.smooth_corners.tip: Rounds the corners of panels, buttons and popups with smooth arcs drawn at your screen's full resolution instead of pixel steps. Off keeps the pixel look.
slate.settings.cursor.tip: The mouse pointer while a menu is open: the system's own, or the same arrow in Slate's colours (light, or in the accent colour) with a hard shadow. It grows with the GUI scale.
slate.settings.translucent_panels.tip: Slate style: rows, cards, lists, panels, popups, menus, tooltips and toasts let what is behind them show through, all alike. Tabs, sidebars and headers stay more solid. Off, every one of them is opaque.
slate.settings.compact_auto_scale.tip: With GUI scale on Auto, use one step smaller than vanilla picks (never below 2). Vanilla takes the largest scale that fits, which is usually too big.
slate.settings.menu_background.tip: Out of a world, what every menu stands on, under a dark veil that lets it only just show through: the loading screens' sky with its drifting motes, the main menu's scene (the one chosen for the Overhaul layout, without its chests and buttons), or the menus' own backgrounds. The Overhaul title screen keeps its own scene.
slate.menu_background.sky.tip: The loading screens' sky at dusk, its motes drifting, behind every menu out of a world.
slate.menu_background.title: Main menu scene
slate.menu_background.title.tip: The Overhaul main menu's scene (the one chosen for it), without its chests and buttons, behind every other menu out of a world.
slate.menu_background.off.tip: The menus draw their own backgrounds out of a world.
slate.settings.startup_scene.tip: What the start-up window shows in the Overhaul layout: the factory, built of Create's blocks (only with Create installed: without it the island is always shown), or a floating island of Minecraft's own blocks that builds itself as the game loads, in the game's own colours and font.
slate.settings.startup_timer.tip: How long the game has been starting, on the start-up window and the loading screen that carries it on, and the time the whole start took in a toast once the game is up. The start-up window follows a change from the next start.
slate.startup.done.title: Game started
slate.settings.container_open.tip: How inventories and containers open from the game. The whole screen moves as one, recipe panels and other mods' inventories included.
slate.settings.restyle.hint: Which other screens get Slate's widgets, backgrounds and tooltips with the custom menu style. Inventories and containers follow the container switch above instead.
slate.settings.reset.title: Reset Slate settings?
slate.settings.reset.body: Every option on this page goes back to its default. Layouts and module settings are kept.
slate.setup.title: Set up Slate
slate.setup.subtitle: Pick how much Slate changes. Everything can be changed later, per menu too.
slate.setup.hint: Change these any time in Slate settings.
slate.setup.layout.desc: Slate's rebuilt menus replace vanilla's: a new title screen with a continue card, world and server lists with search and favourites, a compact pause menu and an options hub. Off: vanilla's own screens and button placement, with a Slate button on the title and pause screens.
slate.setup.style.desc: The dark modern look for every menu: layered panels, an accent colour, pixel-stepped corners. Off: vanilla's stone buttons and panels, still animated.
slate.setup.containers.desc: Inventories, chests, furnaces and other container screens get Slate's panel, sunken slot wells, an accent hover ring and light labels. Off: their own textures. Works with either menu style.
slate.toast.test.title: Notifications work
slate.toast.test.body: This is what a Slate toast looks like. Click to dismiss.
slate.action.arg.name: Name
slate.action.arg.title: Title
slate.layout.vanilla.desc: Minecraft's own screens and button placement, with a Slate button on the title and pause screens.
slate.layout.custom.desc: Slate's rebuilt screens: a title screen with a continue card, world and server lists with search and favourites, a compact pause menu and the options hub.
slate.layout.overhaul.desc: Animated 3D scenes built from real Minecraft blocks, players and items. Needs Slate UI.
slate.style.slate.desc: The dark modern look: layered panels, an accent colour, pixel-stepped corners.
slate.style.vanilla.desc: Vanilla's stone buttons and panels, still animated.
slate.slot.title: Title screen
slate.slot.style_only: Laid out by the mod itself
slate.slot.style_only.slate: Slate's look: its frames, plates, buttons and text colours.
slate.slot.style_only.slate.betterinvent: Its own art in Slate's colours, the accent on what is active.
slate.slot.style_only.vanilla.betterinve: Better Inventory's own Vanilla Style look. Choosing it switches that mod's Vanilla Style resource pack on, and Slate's switches it off again: the game loads its resources anew.
slate.slot.style_only.slate.journeymap.f: The full-screen map, the waypoints, the options and the dialogs in Slate's look: its buttons, plates, labels and tooltips. The theme chosen in JourneyMap is kept for the Vanilla style.
slate.slot.style_only.vanilla.journeymap: JourneyMap's own look, untouched, in the theme chosen in its settings.
slate.slot.style_only.slate.journeymap.m: Slate's frame round the minimap in every shape, its compass and its lines of text on Slate's plates, and the waypoint labels in the world to match.
slate.slot.style_only.vanilla.journeymap: JourneyMap's own minimap, untouched, in the theme chosen in its settings.
slate.slot.unavailable.layout: %s is not available for this menu
slate.module.slate.pitch: The theme, the widget toolkit, the restyle of vanilla screens, the layout editor and the hub.
slate.module.slate_menu.pitch: The rebuilt and the overhauled menus: title, play, pause, options, world creation and the loading screens.
slate.module.slate_config.pitch: One settings screen for the whole game and every mod.
slate.module.slate_multiplayer.pitch: Friends, groups, presence, messages, invites and screen sharing.
slate.module.slate_chat.pitch: The in-game chat rebuilt: channels, media, emotes, history and search.
slate.module.slate_building.pitch: Every block's shapes on a wheel, placement ghosts and a build menu with twenty modes.
slate.module.slate_profile.pitch: Looks and skins, cosmetics, a profile picture and bio, and the account switcher.
slate.module.slate_teams.pitch: Teams with ranks, claims, allies, shared waypoints and pings, shown on your map.
slate.module.slate_quests.pitch: An animated quest book: chapters, quest trees within quests, tasks and rewards shared by your team.
slate.module.slate_crafting.pitch: Every item and recipe beside your inventory, and a crafting tree that follows what you have. A fork of EMI: mods that support EMI support it.
slate.module.slate_server.pitch: Homes, warps and the other travel commands, roles with permissions, moderation and rankings, with a menu for players and one for administrators.
slate.module.slate_bridge.pitch: A Discord bot for the server's chat, both ways: names, faces and role colours, replies and mentions, pictures and GIFs.
slate.module.slate_veinminer.pitch: Hold a key and mine one block to break its whole group: ore veins, trees, tunnels and staircases, with a preview of what will break.
slate.feature_test.title: Feature gates
slate.maps.places.in_world.tip: The places float in the world as well, the way Xaero's Minimap shows its own waypoints there
slate.maps.settings.hidden: Hidden one by one from a pin's right click on a map: switch one on to show it again.
slate.maps.settings.hint: The places Slate puts on Xaero's maps and JourneyMap: homes, warps, the team's home. A group switched off is hidden on every map; one place can be hidden from its pin's right click.
slate.maps.label: %s · %s
slate.maps.dev.rename.title: Rename the place
slate.maps.dev.delete.title: Delete this place?
slate.maps.dev.delete.body: %s is taken off every map. This cannot be undone.
slate.maps.dev.no_ground: The map does not know the ground there
slate.maps.dev.name: Its name
slate.settings.menus.desc: Each menu Slate touches can follow the global layout and style or use its own. A layout a menu cannot show right now is greyed out and says why.
slate.layout.not_yet: No menu has an Overhaul screen yet
slate.slot.held.tip: %s has a layout of its own for this menu, so the game's screen shows here, laid out by it. Choose Custom or Overhaul to show Slate's instead; the reset button gives the menu back.
slate.setup.needs_ui: Install Slate UI to choose the Custom or Overhaul layout; until then every menu is Minecraft's own, in the style chosen below.
slate.setup.no_overhaul_yet: The Overhaul layout appears here once a menu has an Overhaul screen.
slate.setup.preview.menus.caption: Menus · %s layout, %s style
slate.settings.in_config: With Slate Config installed, the layout, the menu style, the container style and the Menus table live on its Interface page.
slate.stage.test.title: Stage test
slate.stage.test.hint: Tab / arrows: focus · Enter: activate · click the chest
slate.stage.test.player_tip: A real skin, posed without an entity
slate.stage.test.cog_tip: A JSON model; hover spins it up
slate.stage.capture.title: Scene capture
slate.stage.capture.singleplayer_only: Scene capture reads saved structures, which only exist in singleplayer
slate.stage.capture.bad_id: Template and scene must be ids like title or slate_menu:title
slate.stage.capture.no_template: No saved structure at %s (save it with a structure block first)
slate.stage.capture.no_origin: Look at the structure block that saved it, or pass the structure's x y z
